clips.send: A friend who gets genuinely furious at every outrage video they watch - a jolt of unease, then the urge to test it themselves.
clips.caption:
The producer doesn't pick a topic because it's true. He picks it because research already proved which words make you feel something.

They test phrases, track which ones trigger fear or outrage, and hand the winning words back to the host to use again next time. Most hosts don't even realize they're doing it - they just know the formula gets clicks and keeps you watching.

Notice how you feel right after the video ends. Crappier than before you pressed play. That's not an accident. That's the business model.

Comment RISE and I'll send you how to spot it before it works on you.

clips.send: A friend who always frames things as what they're trying to avoid instead of what they want - a jolt of recognition, then curiosity about the fix.
clips.caption:
Driving home in bad weather, there are two ways to think about it.

"I don't want to get into an accident" and "I want to get home safe" sound like the same thought. They are not. One keeps your attention locked on the accident. The other points it at the outcome you actually want.

Manifesting runs on where your attention sits, not on good intentions. Say what you want, every time - never what you're trying to avoid.
